public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 59

*References:*
- [E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture59

open SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 59](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

For a simple connected graph $G$, the size $f(G)$ of a largest induced forest
satisfies $f(G) \ge \lceil \sqrt{\mathrm{residue}(G) \cdot b(G)} \rceil$, where
$\mathrm{residue}(G)$ is the Havel-Hakimi residue (the number of zeros remaining
after applying the Havel-Hakimi algorithm to the degree sequence until termination)
and $b(G)$ is the size of a largest induced bipartite subgraph.

See: Favaron, Mahéo, Saclé (1991) for the residue; DeLaVina's Graffiti.pc for the conjecture.

This conjecture is false. There is a connected counterexample on 123 vertices
with `residue G = 101`, `b G = 122`, and `G.largestInducedForestSize = 111`.
Indeed, `101 * 122 = 12322 = 111 ^ 2 + 1`, so the conjectured lower bound is 112.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/QDKStorm/wowii59-counterexample/blob/main/Counterexample59.lean"]
theorem conjecture59 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]
      (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (_ : G.Connected),
      ⌈Real.sqrt ((residue G : ℝ) * b G)⌉ ≤ (G.largestInducedForestSize : ℝ) := by
  sorry

-- Sanity checks

/-- The `largestInducedForestSize` is nonneg. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) : 0 ≤ G.largestInducedForestSize := Nat.zero_le _

/-- The residue of $K_2$ equals $1$: degree sequence is $[1, 1]$; one Havel-Hakimi
step gives $[0]$, leaving a single zero. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example : residue (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) = 1 := by
  simp [residue, Fin.univ_succ, Multiset.sort_cons, residueAux, havelHakimiStep]

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture59

status_issues.recorded: `formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/QDKStorm/wowii59-counterexample/blob/main/Counterexample59.lean"`, alongside `category research solved` and `answer(False)`.
status_issues.source_status: Zhe Zhang (QDKStorm), 23 July 2026, supplies an informal disproof and a partial Lean certificate, not a complete Lean proof of the conjecture's falsity. The negative answer and solved category are supported, but the formal-proof record overstates what the linked artifact proves.
status_issues.evidence: The companion README explicitly says: “The exact values of `b(G)` and `f(G)` are established by the proof above and by the structural certificate verifier; they are not yet fully formalized in Lean” (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QDKStorm/wowii59-counterexample/main/README.md, lines 185–188). The linked Lean file proves connectedness, the degree sequence, residue 101, and the numerical inequality `¬(⌈Real.sqrt ((101 : ℝ) * 122)⌉ ≤ (111 : ℝ))`. It contains no graph-level bipartite-number or forest-number bounds connecting 122 and 111 to those invariants. I compiled the certificate and inspected its theorem types and axioms.
status_issues.suggested_change: Keep `category research solved` and `answer(False)`. Remove the `formal_proof using lean4` attribute until a complete graph-level disproof is available, or point it to such a proof. Retain the README as an ordinary reference for the informal disproof.

reformulations.difference: Lean requires `[Nontrivial α]`, whereas the source states the bound for simple connected graphs without excluding the one-vertex graph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The omitted connected case is K₁, for which residue, bipartite number and largest induced forest size are all 1, so the inequality holds with equality. Thus restricting the universal claim to nontrivial vertex types does not change it or its negation. The equivalence between the universal statements with and without `[Nontrivial α]` was proved as `nontrivial_domain_iff` in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`, without sorry.

sources_consulted: E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjecture 59 and surrounding remarks: https://web.archive.org/web/20260723161800/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/all.html
WOWII definitions 15, 16, 41 and 42 (bipartite number, ceiling, forest number and residue): https://web.archive.org/web/20260723161735/http://cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/wowIIdefs.js

O. Favaron, M. Mahéo and J.-F. Saclé, On the residue of a graph, Journal of Graph Theory 15(1) (1991), 39–64; publisher abstract obtained through https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1002%2Fjgt.3190150107

Local definitions: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Residue.lean and FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Induced.lean; Mathlib definitions of induced graphs, acyclicity, bipartiteness, connectedness and degree.
review.notes: The original formula and all three invariant definitions match the Lean statement. Both anonymous sanity checks are correct. Scratch checks covered empty and small graphs, attainment and boundedness of the forest-size supremum, and equivalence of the real-valued ceiling inequality to the corresponding natural-number squared inequality. The cited certificate compiles without sorry; its residue and degree-sequence computations use native_decide. The archived WOWII page retains its older open label, but the later counterexample's informal argument supports the file's solved status.
